segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Hormuz · Wall Street · Paramount
bullets: Iran, Hormuz and Houthi claims
Record Nasdaq, 5% yields
Paramount-Warner close expected
Measles and a heat wave

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Tuesday, October sixth.
Today: Iran says it controls the Strait of Hormuz, Houthis claim strikes on Saudi sites, and Wall Street hits a record with yields above five percent.
Plus a giant media merger, a measles outbreak, and a heat wave out West. Let's go.

segments.strap: IRAN: HORMUZ CONTROLLED; HOUTHIS CLAIM SAUDI STRIKES
segments.headline: Hormuz and the Gulf

graphic.title: Hormuz and the Gulf
bullets: Euronews: Iran says it retains full control
Rial at record low; oil minister reported to resign
Houthis claim Saudi airport and Aramco strikes
Pakistan: talks show 'significant progress'

lines.text: Euronews reports Iran's military says it keeps full control of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's foreign minister says the strait could reopen within seven days if Tehran's conditions are met.
The same report says Iran's oil minister resigned, and the rial hit a record low. Those are reports, not confirmed by us.
Reuters reports the Houthis claim attacks on Saudi sites, including King Khalid airport, an Aramco refinery at Rabigh, and Abha airport. Saudi Arabia had not confirmed them.

Pakistan says U.S.-Iran talks are ongoing, with significant progress. It also says Hormuz is a point of serious disagreement. And the A.P. says Trump attributed the return of B-1 bombers from Britain to an Iran-linked threat. That is his account.

graphic.title: Oil, early Tuesday
bullets: Reuters quotes, 00:03 GMT
G7 reserve releases eased supply worries
Middle East exports above pre-war levels
Another early read: Brent $99.07

lines.text: Reuters has Brent at one hundred dollars and twenty-eight cents early today, and U.S. crude at eighty-nine thirty-three. An A.P. morning report had Brent a little lower, at ninety-nine oh seven.
Reuters says G7 reserve releases and strong Middle East exports eased supply worries, while Houthi attacks keep Gulf risks in view.

graphic.title: Monday's close
bullets: Nasdaq at a record (A.P.)
S&P within 0.3% of its record
Nikkei +1.1%; Kospi -0.9%
Bitcoin ~$85,800 at Monday's close

lines.text: The A.P. reports the S and P five hundred rose seven tenths of a percent, to seven thousand seven hundred seventy-four. The Nasdaq rose one point one percent to a record, twenty-seven thousand four hundred seventy-seven.

The Dow gained two tenths, to fifty-one thousand two hundred sixty-eight. The ten-year Treasury yield reached five point three one percent. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei rose one point one percent, and South Korea's Kospi fell nine tenths, with chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix down.

Last week's jobs report showed twenty-nine thousand new jobs, far below forecasts. Odds of an October Fed hike depend on who is counting. One read has about seventy-seven percent for no move. Another outlet headlines fifty-fifty. That conflict is unresolved.
Bitcoin closed Monday near eighty-five thousand eight hundred dollars, per StatMuse.

segments.strap: PARAMOUNT-WARNER BROS. CLOSE EXPECTED TODAY; WEISS TO CBS NEWS
segments.headline: Paramount and Warner Bros.

graphic.title: A $110 billion media deal
bullets: Combined company to be called Skydance
Mark Thompson to lead CNN Worldwide
Bari Weiss to lead CBS News
Closing not yet confirmed

lines.text: Paramount Skydance's purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery is expected to close today, according to NBC News and Paramount's own release. The price is thirty-one dollars a share in cash, about one hundred ten billion dollars in all.
Paramount says the combined company will be called Skydance. Mark Thompson is named to lead CNN Worldwide, and Bari Weiss to lead CBS News. We have not seen the closing itself yet.

segments.strap: TRUMP EASES RED-DYED DIESEL LIMITS; GAS COSTS WORRY HALF OF ADULTS
segments.headline: Fuel, food and farms

graphic.title: Prices and the midterms
bullets: Order eases limits on tax-free red-dyed diesel (A.P.)
Signed at a Nebraska campaign stop
AP-NORC: about half highly concerned about gas costs, up from 39% in July
About half also concerned about food

lines.text: The A.P. reports President Trump signed an order temporarily easing limits on red-dyed diesel, the tax-free fuel used off-road, including on farms. He said it would lower costs for farmers and for goods.
He signed it in Grand Island, Nebraska, while campaigning for Senator Pete Ricketts against independent Dan Osborn.
An A.P.-NORC poll finds about half of Americans are highly concerned about affording gasoline. In July it was thirty-nine percent. About half are also highly concerned about food.

segments.strap: OPENAI BEGINS BILLING FOR GPT-ROSALIND; SEC OKS 3X CRYPTO ETFS
segments.headline: Tech and crypto rules

graphic.title: A.I. pricing, crypto approvals
bullets: GPT-Rosalind: approved life-sciences research only
SEC order dated Oct. 2: Cboe 3x Bitcoin, Ether ETFs
No launch date yet
Coinbase ALEO delay resolved

lines.text: OpenAI's changelog says billing for its GPT-Rosalind research model began Monday. Five dollars per million input tokens, twenty-five dollars per million output tokens. Access is for approved life-sciences research.

Yahoo Finance reports the S.E.C. approved Cboe listings for three-times-leveraged Bitcoin and Ether funds. The order is dated October second. The funds still need registration, and no launch date was reported.
And Coinbase says delays in sending and receiving the ALEO token were resolved Monday. Buying, selling and fiat transfers were not affected.

segments.strap: PENNSYLVANIA MEASLES: 1,004 CASES; RUSSIA HOSPITAL QUARANTINED
segments.headline: Health watch

graphic.title: Measles and a Siberian quarantine
bullets: Pennsylvania outbreak since April (A.P.)
Siberian institute employee died of unknown pneumonia
Authorities: no evidence her work caused it
Plague rumors unconfirmed

lines.text: Pennsylvania officials count one thousand four cases of measles in an outbreak since April, with one hundred ninety-eight hospitalizations and five deaths, the A.P. reports. The latest national C.D.C. figure is nearly thirty-nine hundred.

Separately, the A.P. reports Russian authorities quarantined a hospital after an employee of a Siberian anti-plague institute died of pneumonia of unknown cause. Officials say there is no evidence the pathogens she studied caused it. Plague rumors are unconfirmed.

segments.strap: CALIFORNIA HEAT 15-20° ABOVE NORMAL; FLORIDA HEAVY RAIN RISK
segments.headline: Heat and rain

graphic.title: Heat out West, rain in Florida
bullets: Heat advisories in California through Oct. 8
Heavy-rain risk lingers in Florida
Cooler air across Great Lakes, Northeast

lines.text: The Weather Prediction Center forecasts a late-season heat wave in central and southern California and the Great Basin, fifteen to twenty degrees above normal.
Florida keeps a heavy-rain risk. Cooler air crosses the Great Lakes and the Northeast.

segments.strap: UIC MEDICAL COLLEGE RANSOMWARE; EXCHANGE FLAW NEEDS PATCH
segments.headline: Cyber watch

graphic.title: Ransomware and an Exchange bug
bullets: UIC College of Medicine systems disrupted
UIC: systems restored, some information stolen
Patient care and main network unaffected
Exchange CVE-2026-96940: on-premises servers must patch

lines.text: Recorded Future News reports ransomware disrupted systems at the University of Illinois Chicago's medical college. The school says the systems are restored, some information was stolen, and patient care was not affected.

And The Hacker News reports a flaw in Microsoft Exchange, tracked as C.V.E. twenty twenty-six, ninety-six nine forty, could let a signed-in user read other mailboxes in the same organization. Microsoft says Exchange Online is fixed. On-premises servers need the patch.

segments.strap: FALCON 9 SDA LAUNCH SLIPS TO OCT. 8; VERITY LEADS BOX OFFICE
segments.headline: Space and the box office

graphic.title: Launch tracker, weekend film
bullets: Falcon 9 SDA mission now listed Oct. 8, 07:54 UTC
SpaceX page still showed an earlier date
Box office figures are estimates

lines.text: A launch tracker now lists SpaceX's Falcon 9 mission for the Space Development Agency for October eighth, after the October sixth target passed. SpaceX's own page still showed an earlier date, so treat it as a claim.
Box Office Mojo lists Verity at thirty-two point six million dollars for the weekend, and Digger at eight million. Both are estimates.
